Anita / team —

Thanks for the MAUP. I mocked up three practical configurations (attached: redwood_capacity_options.pdf) with estimates and trade-offs. TL;DR below. Lead times assume our current procurement windows and available rack capacity in SIN region.

Option A — Narrow-sustained (recommended if budget-sensitive):
- 12 A100 80GB GPUs (prod nodes), no burst lane.
- Sustained throughput: covers 95% of your steady-state based on provided multipliers.
- Lead time: 6–8 weeks for dedicated reservations in SIN.
- Estimated committed monthly: USD 78,000.
- Pros: lower committed cost, simpler ops. Cons: limited headroom for 3x spikes.

Option B — Sustained + burst buffer (balanced):
- 12 A100 80GB GPUs + 6 burst-capacity H100-enabled nodes available via routed burst lane (on-demand for spikes).
- Sustained throughput with 2–3x peak coverage via burst.
- Lead time: 6–10 weeks (burst depends on regional spare capacity).
- Estimated committed monthly: USD 112,000 (commit) + burst metering.
- Pros: predictable baseline with elastic handling of spikes. Cons: complexity in routing and slightly higher cost.

Option C — Aggressive headroom (fast growth):
- 20 H100 GPUs (mixed H100/A100 pool to maximize perf on long-seq workloads).
- Lead time: 10–14 weeks; procurement risk if H100 supply tight.
- Estimated committed monthly: USD 180,000.
- Pros: runway for rapid scale and higher SLO headroom. Cons: biggest up-front commitment and cost.

Cross-region fallback notes:
- EU fallback (Frankfurt) is possible for queued requests; we advise routing only non-PII flows to EU. Network egress and added latency will apply.
- We can offer KV/prefix cache warmup policies to reduce cold-start costs when failing over.

Compliance/security contact: David Kim will own the security questionnaire and can supply SOC2 artifacts and our region-specific data residency controls.

Action items I need from Crestwave:
1) Confirm node preference (A100 vs H100)
2) Provide sample 7-day histogram or at least 24-hr RPS by bucket
3) Procurement target date (preferred signature window)

I included a short cost/lead-time table in redwood_capacity_options.pdf to make selection easier.

Thanks,
Irene
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
